evidence: The Alternative.me Fear & Greed Index currently stands at 22 ('Extreme Fear'), dipping slightly from 23 the prior day. While sentiment has rebounded from deep single-digit lows recorded a week prior (reaching as low as 8 on June 8), the entire 7-day average (17.14) and 30-day average (20.17) indicate protracted negative market sentiment. Sustained extreme fear can indicate potential seller exhaustion and mean-reversion bounces; however, over a strict 24-hour horizon without decisive positive sentiment momentum, the market remains fragile and susceptible to continuation of the prevailing downtrend. Consequently, the probability of an upward move is evaluated near neutral with a slight downward bias.
limitations: Fear & Greed Index readings update daily and inherently lag real-time spot price movements.
Extreme fear states can persist over extended periods without immediate price reversals.
Snapshot availability and later revisions are caller-attested, not independently verified.
